definitions.person: An expressed human name, description or reference serving as a task participant, queried subject, recipient, beneficiary, or owner whose possession identifies a request-relevant object, account or content. Pure conversational self-reference or assistant address alone is insufficient. Apply request-relevant scope.
definitions.media_type: An expressed kind or format of content, or an explicitly used source/channel for obtaining, carrying or publishing content. A platform name counts only with evidence of this content-channel role, not merely application access, company identity or account metadata. Apply request-relevant scope.

person: A possessive can establish a human owner when that ownership identifies the requested object or content: my audiobook, my playlist, my inbox and my calendar follow the same rule. A proper name or recovered identity is not required.

Require the owner/participant role to be supported as human. Corporate ownership or ambiguous its/their without human evidence does not automatically establish person. Assistant ownership alone is not a human reference.
I want, please tell me, and direct assistant address alone are conversational framing, not an additional person role. Explicit recipients, beneficiaries, subjects or owners can independently qualify.

Ownership does not automatically imply personal_info, relation or authorship; these types require their own field, interpersonal-role or creator evidence. My audiobook need not be authored by the speaker.
media_type: Explicit content formats and kinds such as audiobook, podcast, news, picture or video can count independently of a particular work identity.

A named service counts as a media source/channel when the utterance expresses content obtained from, played through, or published on it. Posting on Twitter and checking posts on Facebook establish this role; the same mention may independently satisfy app_name.

Opening an application alone, a company stock-price query, a contact handle lookup, profile metadata, login status or a bare platform name does not by itself express a media-source/channel role. Do not infer it from native intent or a platform dictionary.

Separate source from subject: news about a company is not evidence that the company is the news provider. Platform/topic or station/app ambiguity remains unavailable when the full utterance cannot settle the role.
No implication from app_name to media_type or vice versa is allowed. Dual presence is supported by two explicit roles, not inferred from real-world corporate identity or native label overlap.

reading: All278 owner-pattern and155 platform-pattern learning references read; fixed diagnostic searches, not exhaustive type populations or labeling rules.

upstream_evidence.interpretation: Human participant examples and explicit BBC/radio/Facebook channels support role distinctions. Possessive-owner extension and dual predicates are project semantic choices, not identical native tagging.

scope: Input role definition shared across tasks; no query-specific question routing, output-value generation or identity lookup.
